correctness.rationale: Correctness PASS. Summing the exact balanced May–Leonard equations (alpha+beta=2) gives logistic S'=S(1-S), S>0 for nonzero nonnegative starting data. On the simplex, p_i'=-(alpha-1)S p_i(p_{i+1}-p_{i+2})+mu(1-3p_i). Entropy H=-sum log(3p_i) has exact H'=-mu(sum 1/p_i-9), strictly negative outside p=e, and mutation pushes boundary states immediately interior, yielding global frequency convergence. Writing u=p-e, B_i=-(u_(i+1)-u_(i+2))/3, B²|E=-I/3 and u'=-3mu u+(alpha-1)S Bu+(alpha-1)S N(u), N quadratic. For nonzero u, logarithmic radial slope -3mu+O(||u||) yields an integrable correction and a positive limit L=lim exp(3mu t)||u||. Removing exact rotation R=exp((alpha-1) B tau) gives convergent nonzero vector v with error O(exp(-3mu t)); restore O(exp(-6mu t)). Orthogonal split x-e=(S-1)1/3+S u gives the sharp crossover at mu=1/3, with S0=1 and p0=e correctly exceptional. Six independently chosen rational configurations checked mass/frequency/entropy identities exactly, not finite proof of globality.
